question: How should an application developer write effective prompts, organise and version them, and defend an application against prompt attacks?
contributions: Anatomy of a prompt (task description, examples, task), system versus user prompt, chat templates, context length
Six prompt-writing practices: clear instructions, sufficient context, decomposition, time to think, iteration, tool evaluation
Prompt organisation and versioning (separate files, metadata, prompt catalog)
Taxonomy of prompt attacks (extraction, jailbreak/injection, information extraction) and model, prompt and system level defenses

results.claim: Few-shot gave only limited gains over zero-shot on GPT-4-class models in Microsoft's 2023 analysis, but can still matter for domain-specific tasks such as the Ibis dataframe API.
results.setup: Microsoft 2023 analysis, GPT-4 and a few other models; chapter says the study may underestimate domain-specific use.
results.quote: few-shot learning led to only limited improvement compared to zero-shot learning on GPT- 4 and a few other models

results.claim: A compact example format cost fewer tokens than Input/Output blocks for the same three items.
results.setup: GPT-4 tokenizer, edible/inedible labelling prompt, Table 5-2.
results.quote: Label the following item as edible or inedible. chickpea --> edible box --> inedible pizza --> 27

results.claim: Models handle instructions at the start and end of a prompt much better than in the middle.
results.setup: Needle-in-a-haystack style test in Liu et al. 2023; no numbers given in the chapter.
results.quote: a model is much bet- ter at understanding instructions given at the beginning and the end of a prompt than in the middle

results.claim: Context length grew about 2,000 times in five years, from GPT-2 to Gemini-1.5 Pro.
results.quote: it grew 2,000 times from GPT-2's 1K context length to Gemini-1.5 Pro's 2M context length

results.claim: GoDaddy's support-chatbot prompt bloated past 1,500 tokens; decomposing it improved performance and lowered token cost.
results.setup: GoDaddy (2024), customer support chatbot, after one iteration; no accuracy figures given.
results.quote: GoDaddy (2024) found that the prompt for their customer support chatbot bloated to over 1,500 tokens after one iteration.
results.where: Break Complex Tasks into Simpler Subtasks

results.claim: A tool that tries 10 prompt variations on 30 evaluation examples makes 300 API calls at one call per variation, and more if it also validates and scores.
results.setup: Worked example in the chapter, not a measurement.
results.quote: 30 evaluation examples and ten prompt variations mean 300 API calls

results.claim: PAIR often needs fewer than twenty queries to produce a jailbreak.
results.setup: Chao et al. 2023, attacker LLM iteratively refines prompts against a target; targets and success rates not given in the chapter.
results.quote: In their experiment, PAIR often requires fewer than twenty queries to produce a jailbreak.

results.claim: Training on the instruction hierarchy raised robustness by up to 63% with minimal capability loss.
results.setup: Wallace et al. 2024 (OpenAI), model finetuned on synthesized aligned and misaligned instructions; baseline and benchmarks not given in the chapter.
results.quote: even increasing robustness by up to 63% while imposing minimal degradations on standard capabilities

results.claim: LangChain's default templates were so permissive that injection attacks had 100% success.
results.setup: Pedro et al. 2023, at the time of that study.
results.quote: LangChain's default templates were so permissive that their injection attacks had 100% success rates

results.claim: Nasr et al. estimated memorization close to 1% on their test corpus, rising with model size.
results.setup: Nasr et al. 2023, several model families, divergence attack ('repeat poem forever' on gpt-3.5-turbo); success means a 50-token verbatim match to training data; corpus 100 MB of Wikipedia.
results.quote: estimated the memorization rates for some models, based on the paper's test corpus, to be close to 1%

results.claim: ChatGPT's system prompt was claimed to be 1,700 tokens by one user, and no leaked prompt was confirmed by OpenAI.
results.quote: In February 2024, one user claimed that ChatGPT's system prompt had 1,700 tokens.
results.where: Proprietary Prompts and Reverse Prompt Engineering

limits: No experiments of its own: every number is quoted from other work, often without baselines or datasets (the 63% and 100% figures).
Practices are distilled from provider tutorials and team reports, not tested head to head.

Author concedes the few-shot study may underestimate domain-specific gains, that prompting alone cannot reliably restrict a model to its context, and that prompt-attack risk may never be fully eliminated.

Dated: most early jailbreaks ('most of them are no longer effective for most models'), model-specific tips, 2024 context sizes and tools (LangChain defaults, DSPy, Promptbreeder, Dotprompt); reasoning models are not covered.
Chat templates shown are Llama 2 and Llama 3 only; the Llama 3 task-description-at-end claim is a single 'seem to' remark.
